steps.title: 3 Therefore, the present study will...
steps.instruction: 3 Therefore, the present study will aime to assess the quality of care of early versus 36 delayed feeding after ESD. 37 38 2. Methods 39 We followed the Preferred reporting items for systematic review and meta-analysis 40 protocols (PRISMA-P) 2015 for preparing this protocol [22]. We will publish this 41 protocol in protocols.io (https://www.protocols.io/) 42 Inclusion criteria of the articles for review 43 Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) will be included to assess the effecticacy and 44 safety of early versus delayed feeding after ESD. All studies will be included, reported 45 as full text, those published as abstract only, and unpublished data, regardless of 46 language or country restrictions. Inclusion criteria will be adult patients (≥ 18 years of 47 age) who underwent ESD for gastric lesions. Exclusion criteria will be residual and 48 recurrent lesions after ESD. 49 Type of outcomes 50 Primary outcomes will be post-ESD bleeding, patients’ satisfaction, and lengths of 51 hospital stay (days). Post-ESD bleeding will be defined as clinical evidence of bleeding 52 after ESD, as represented by hematemesis, melena, or hematochezia after normalization 53

steps.title: 4 of stool color, or a...
steps.instruction: 4 of stool color, or a decrease in hemoglobin levels of ≥2.0 g/dL, after consecutive stable 54 hemoglobin level and/or active bleeding confirmed by endoscopic evaluation. Patients’ 55 satisfaction will be defined as the mean score of the numeric rating scale for allover 56 patients’ satisfaction after ESD. The lowest score corresponds to no very dissatisfaction 57 while the highest score corresponds to very satisfaction. Secondary outcomes will be 58 abdominal pains and post-ESD ulcer healing status, and all adverse events. Abdominal 59 pain will be defined as the mean score of the numeric rating scale for patients’ 60 abdominal pain after ESD. The lowest score corresponds to no pain while the highest 61 score corresponds to unbearable pain. Post-ESD ulcer healing status will be defined as 62 proportion of patients with ulcer stage S1 and S2 by follow-up 63 esophagogastroduodenoscopy at 2 months after ESD. All adverse events will be defined 64 by the original articles. 65 Search method 66 The following databases will be searched: the Cochrane Central Resister of Controlled 67 Trials (CENTRAL), MEDLINE via Ovid, and EMBASE via ProQuest Dialog 68 (Appendix 1). The following databases will be also searched for ongoing or unpublished 69 trials: the World Health Organization International Clinical Trials Platform Search 70 Portal (ICTRP), and ClinicalTrials.gov (Appendix 2). The reference lists will be 71

steps.title: 5 checked for studies, including international...
steps.instruction: 5 checked for studies, including international guidelines published by the American 72 Gastroenterological Association, the European Society of Gastrointestinal Endoscopy, 73 and Japan Gastroenterological Endoscopy Society [4, 11, 15], as well as the reference 74 lists of eligible studies and articles citing eligible studies. The original authors for 75 unpublished or additional data will be asked if necessary. 76 Data collection and analysis 77 Two reviewers (Jun W and Joji W) will independently screen titles and abstracts, 78 followed by the assessment of the eligibility based on the full texts. If relevant data is 79 missing, the original authors will be contacted. Disagreements between the two 80 reviewers will be resolved by discussion, and if this failed, a third reviewer (KK) acted 81 as an arbiter. 82 Two reviewers (Jun W and Joji W) will independently perform data extraction of the 83 included studies using standardized data collection form, including the information on 84 study design, study population, patients’ characteristics, primary and secondary 85 outcomes. The risk of bias will be independently evaluated using the Risk of Bias 2 86 [23]. Any disagreements will be resolved by discussion, and if failed, a third reviewer 87 (KK) acted as an arbiter, if necessary. 88

steps.title: 6 We will pool the relative...
steps.instruction: 6 We will pool the relative risk ratios and the 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for the 89 following binary variables: post-ESD bleeding and post-ESD ulcer healing status. We 90 will pool the mean differences (MD) and the 95% CIs for the lengths of hospital stay. 91 We will pool the standard mean differences (SMD) and the 95% CIs for patients’ 92 satisfaction and abdominal pains. If some scales increase with patients’ satisfaction 93 while others decreased, it multiplies the mean values from one set of studies by -1 to 94 ensure that all the scales point in the same direction. The intention-to-treat (ITT) 95 analysis will be performed for all dichotomous data as much as possible. For, 96 continuous data, missing data will not impute based on the recommendation by 97 Cochrane handbook [24]. Meta-analysis will be performed about the available data in 98 the original study. 99 Missing outcomes 100 When original studies only report standard error or p value, the standard deviation will 101 be calculated based on the method by Altman [25]. If these values is missing when the 102 original author was contacted, the standard deviation will be calculated by the CI and 103 the t value based on the method by the Cochrane handbook [24], or validated method 104 [26]. Validity of these methods will be analyzed by sensitivity analysis. 105 Assessment of heterogeneity 106

steps.title: 7 The heterogeneity will be evaluated...
steps.instruction: 7 The heterogeneity will be evaluated by visual inspection of the forest plots and 107 calculating the I2 statistic (I2 values of 0% to 40%: might not be important; 30% to 60%: 108 may represent moderate heterogeneity; 75% to 100%: considerable heterogeneity) [24]. 109 When heterogeneity is identified (I2 > 50%), the reason of heterogeneity will be 110 assessed using subgroup analysis. 111 Assessment of reporting bias 112 When more than 10 trials are pooled, a funnel plot will be created and examined to 113 explore possible publication biases. Egger test will be performed as well. When less 114 than 10 trials, the test will be not performed [24]. 115 Meta-analysis 116 Meta-analysis will be performed using Review Manager software (The Cochrane 117 Collaboration, Copenhagen, Denmark) and will be used a random-effects model. 118 Subgroup analysis 119 We will evaluate the subgroup analyses of the primary outcomes in patients with lesion 120 size (< 20 mm versus ≥ 20 mm) when sufficient data were available. 121 Sensitivity analysis 122

steps.title: 8 The following sensitivity analyses of...
steps.instruction: 8 The following sensitivity analyses of the primary outcomes will be undertaken: 123 exclusion of studies using imputed statistics, and missing participants: verify the 124 robustness of the results by seeking informative missingness odds ratios [26]. 125 Summary of findings table 126 Summary of finding table will be made for the primary and secondary outcome based 127 on the Cochrane handbook [24]. The study quality will be assessed using the Grading of 128 Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach [27]. 129 130 3.
